meta.title: The Old Town Trail Map
meta.textType: functional: a map with a key and directions

paragraphs: On Saturday, September twenty-sixth, the Explorers walked a trail in the old town. The trail was two kilometers long. It started at the bus stop. Teacher Kim read the directions from a card, and the children listened. "Go north to the bridge," she said. "After you cross the bridge, turn west." Lily wrote the first two directions in her notebook.

The children walked north on a quiet road to the bridge. A sign on the bridge said, "NO BIKES ON THE BRIDGE." After the bridge, they turned west and came to a big road. There was a traffic light at the crossing. "Before you cross, look at the light," said Teacher Kim. "Use the crossing when the light is green." Leo waited for the green light. Then all the children crossed.

On the other side, the café was opposite the post office. It was also close to the crossing. A sign on the counter said, "JUICE: TWENTY BAHT." "How much is the juice?" asked Mia. "Twenty baht," said the woman at the counter. "What time does the café close?" asked Leo. "At six o'clock," said the woman. Mia paid with two coins, and she drank her juice.

After the café, Teacher Kim gave the last directions. "Go south to the market," she said. "Then go east to the old library." The market was busy, but the children kept going. At the old library, Teacher Kim asked, "Can you find the finish?" "There it is!" said Lily. She pointed at a green flag on the door.

That afternoon, Leo and Mia drew the trail map at Lily's table. Leo drew the roads and the buildings. Mia added a key. The key had five numbers. Number one was the bus stop, and number two was the bridge. Number three was the café, and number four was the market. Number five was the old library, and it was the finish. Lily checked the map with her finger and her notebook. "The café is opposite the post office on the map, too," she said. "This map is ready for the blog."
